page: Microsoft Azure E32pds_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine built on Microsoft Neoverse-N2 ARM processors. The instance provides 32 dedicated physical cores operating at 3.4 GHz with single-threaded execution, backed by a 128 MB L3 cache. Memory capacity is provisioned at 256.0 GB, establishing an 8 GB per vCPU ratio. Local high-speed storage is integrated directly, supplying 1890 GB of NVMe SSD capacity, alongside support for Azure Premium Storage. The instance does not include a discrete GPU accelerator.

Benchmark results demonstrate high throughput in data-intensive tasks. Large-block memory operations place in the top tier of evaluated hardware, reaching 449.0 GB/sec read and 188.31 GB/sec write bandwidth. PassMark database operations and overall memory testing also score in the top ten percent. Multi-threaded processing shows solid scalability, with Geekbench multi-core achieving 20,088 and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression sustaining 339.89 GB/sec. Conversely, single-thread performance benchmarks register within mid-tier percentiles, and large-scale language model prompt evaluation exhibits lower throughput.

The 1:8 core-to-memory ratio paired with fast local NVMe storage delivers high resource density for memory-bound applications without the overhead of unneeded compute hyper-threading. The dedicated core architecture offers predictable concurrency. Microsoft Azure E32pds_v6 is engineered for in-memory caching systems, distributed relational or NoSQL database clusters, real-time analytics engines, and memory-heavy CI/CD compilation workloads.
